Woking community hospital had a fantastic service. If you needed a blood test you could queue from 7 am in the morning. It was particularly useful if you had to fast the night before. I recently had to have a blood test which I had to wait 2 weeks for. Im sure my doctors surgery must be under increased pressure with more flats being built in woking and having to do more blood testing. Apparently Woking community will close at some point. I cant understand why such a fantastic little hospital is being closed down.

Our TIs that help out on the ward offer us a variety of activities when they are helping out on the ward. One example is my birthday, where we had really good celebrations, so all thanks to them. They make the best of this current situation.

They always get us involved in activities \nI have enjoyed playing board games and going out walking and doing karaoke and just having casual chats. \nThey always encourage people to join in stuff, for example bingo, quizzes, keep fit in the garden.

I was given the telephone number by my GP practice one day in May 2020. I was having a tightness and heaviness and some pain in my chest. I phoned the hospital at 11am and a nurse took information from me. I was given an appointment at 12.15 that day for The Cardiac investigation hub.I was seen on time had a ECG ,blood test and other tests done by two medical staff. The results came back about one and a half hours later. Thankfully everything was ok .I was given a lot of information about the results and came away feeling confident .I was also told not to hesitate if I ever felt anyway like this again to seek advice.A very reassuring experience .

Theyve kept us motivated and occupied us when we were struggling.
Its really helped us with lockdown to stay tocuies and positive. They continue to work hard and do their job.
Many thanks to all the TIs - theyve really helped us when we needed them most.

I am based in England but was having a tough pregnancy with a few issues so decided to visit my parents in Argyll for a fortnights break at the start of March (2020) at 32 weeks. Then Covid-19 happened and I got stuck - for want of a better word - in the area as things started to get serious and ultimately lockdown was imposed. It was a stressful time as I only had a small hold-all of clothes with me for me and my two-and-a-half-year-old daughter. Moreover, my husband was at our house, several hundred miles away. (Luckily he made it up just before lockdown). I never for a second thought I would have the baby away from home as I assumed the situation would calm down relatively quickly, allowing me to go back in time. Of course it didnt and the decision was taken out of my hands.Despite the unconventional situation, I could not have had a more positive experience, however, both in terms of the care I received from the midwives at Mid-Argyll Hospital in Lochgilphead (Both Karens, Brenda, Nicky, Donna) and at RAH in Paisley. I would also like to mention by name Claire, a midwife based at the Princess Royal who was drafted in to help out during a very busy night for the labour ward. She was the one who actually delivered my baby.I was put at ease within minutes of my first encounter with the mid-Argyll team and incredibly well looked after throughout. I had my son at the beginning of May 2020, 11 days late in Paisley. I had a very traumatic experience with my daughter (down south) for various reasons. This time round, although labour was long and I required some repair work (to put it as nicely as possible) afterwards, was completely different.The after-care was similarly excellent. I would have been impressed in normal times, but to have experienced such kindness and professionalism amid the unprecedented circumstances in which we find ourselves was truly humbling.  I cant quite get my head around the fact that these pivotal life moments, such as giving birth, are populated by people you wont necessarily come across ever again. Total strangers effectively, there in your hour of need.With that in mind, Id just like to say that, although our paths may have crossed only briefly, we will remember forever all you did for us and the lengths you went to to keep us safe. For that, we thank you from the bottom of our hearts.
We have had some great staff from DRC & Ted coming onto wards.\nThey are bringing craft stuff and playing games\nIt has been great as all patients who want to get involved can - even seg patients
We played Bingo and did a ward quiz\nI am in segregation and was allowed to get involved. It was really nice to feel included in ward activity.
Its been good having sessions on ward, because DRC is closed.\nThe staff are very nice and make the activities for us.\nIt passes time and helps staff out on ward
I love the DRC staff\nThey make us do stuff that is fun
From bingo to compound karaoke to bringing round a pop shop the TIs have kept us sane during this lockdown. When on wards with us they also play games and do quizzes.\nBig Thanks to all of them :)

After contracting COVID-19, I spent 4 weeks in FVRH ICU, three weeks of which I was on a ventilator. During this time, I received the highest possible level of nursing and professional care, and I absolutely acknowledge that it was only due to this incredible team that I was able to return home. The care I received was nothing short of outstanding; regulations dictated that my family could not be by my bedside in hospital but the staff were able to incorporate small reminders of home throughout my time in hospital, and frequently gave me updates from my family and friends. Nothing was too much trouble, andthe staff went above and beyond anything I could have expected to keep me connected to my loved ones, and made it possible to have my wife and sons virtually by my side. This high-quality care was also extended to my family, who were kept informed and involved in all stages of my recovery process. I cant express enoughhow wonderful this team is, and will always remember the people who saved my life.

My brother was in CCU requiring ventilation and renal dialysis for 3 weeks. He was given a tracheotomy once intubation was discontinued. He came home last week after 7 weeks in Preston Royal. The wonderful staff saved his life - they didnt give up on him. On behalf of his family we want to say thank you so much, please stay safe and strong.

I was recently admitted to ward A12 where I was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis and I have to say a huge thank you to the staff who cared for me. Being in there alone with no visitors and getting that news was a very difficult couple of days and the staff were so caring and attentive! Nothing was too much trouble for them! Must say an extra special thank you to staff nurse Sarah and student nurse Sarah who looked after me with such care that I didnt feel alone at such an upsetting time. The care I received was absolutely second to none!

I am a service user at High Wycombe and I am finding all the online Microsoft Teams groups with One Recovery are working very well and I feel very supported. The groups are very similar to being in person, it did take a little time to get used to but I am now confident and very happy with how it all works. All I can say is positive feedback and nothing negative about these groups. I attend at least one group a day including Art, Peer Support, Relapse Prevention, Service User Plus, Recovery Cafe and occasionally meditation group.
I had to go for a CT scan and cannot thank the staff enough for their empathy and care. Respect to you all x

Would like to say a big thank you to all staff on ward 22B of Forth Valley Royal Hospital I was admitted for emergency surgery and was looked after excellently by all the staff in ICU, and on the ward, the surgeons and Doctors did an excellent job as did the nurses and all the other staff looked after me great which aided to me having a speed recovery and getting home to my family and friends, all staff are working really hard under very busy and stressful times and they have got the management of covid 19 patients and non infected patients down to a T they are stringent in ensure all guidelines are followed in every way and always make time to chat and make sure your ok, thank you all, carol

I would just like to take a moment to express my heartfelt thanks to all the staff on glen more ward at coathill hospital. Especially Leanne, Paula and carol Anne who have looked after my great uncle and catered for his every need. they have went above and beyond to ensure he was comfortable, settled and during this time where we cannot visit they have kept us fully informed every day. I would like to personally thank the staff nurse Leanne who we have built up such a relationship with. What a fantastic nurse and especially when she had to call to break that horrible news to us she was so sympathetic and caring. we will be forever in your debt. Couldnt recommend this unit and the staff enough.

My mum had been attending choir and tai-chi at the hospice before going on the 12 week out-patient programme which she absolutely loved. Covid interrupted this but staff continued to call once a week. During the first 7 weeks of lockdown, mum lived with our family but as her care needs increased dramatically she sadly had to be placed in care. This has been a roller-coaster of emotions for all of us and the calls from staff at the hospice were welcomes. Staff understood and empathised and this was invaluable at times. Thank you for your care.

After reading another positive review on here, I wanted to share my experience too. I felt really listened to and informed my whole pregnancy and supported in my choices by my midwives Kate and then Rosie. Kate helped me feel empowered to choose what was best for me and to know my rights. Rosie provided continual care as well as yoga and hypnobirthing and was very caring and supportive when I got a bit upset after speaking to the obstetrician whose words unintentionally had me doubting my own decision making skills. She took me through my previous birth minute by minute which was exactly what I needed. In the end I am so so thankful to have been able to give birth in Oban hospital - it was a healing experience and took away that lack of control and doubt from my first birth. Miaread was incredible in her unflappable, unobtrusive and intuitive support during labour. The nurse who put in my cannula (though I wasnt able to speak to her by this point) was also really calming and friendly and helped turn around something I was initially afraid of and reluctant to do. I truly couldnt have asked for a better birth experience and never thought I would get the gentle and empowered experience that I did.

Upon arrival I was greeted by the loveliest blonde lady , I think Linda , who made me feel completely at ease .I was so worked up thinking I was wasting NHS time ...I was them met By Staff Nurse Carol Ann who was also incredibly kind and amazing !What a lovely lovely girl and so suited to her job title .My care was 1st class and I cannot thank both girls enough for there careCarol Ann you are amazing , thank you again so so much for your Kindness and concern...I have broken my shoulder ...I will be most definitely be sharing my story ...I LOVE THE NHS ....

My mother was admitted to KGH at the beginning of May 2020 for a period of 2 days before she sadly died.The staff have lost her personal belongings, including her clothes, dentures and a sentimental gold necklace with a crucifix on that she never took off.Proceedures were not followed regarding listing patients valuables. The staff were negligent with her personal belongings. When attempts were made to contact the wards involved everyone shirked responsibility, we were even made out to be lying! We were treated with contempt, and laughed at, certainly not how youre expected to be treated, especially not when mourning for a loved one gone so suddenly.

I felt desperate. My emotions were out of control. I couldnt focus on anything. The aniexty was affecting every aspect of my life. But since having counselling I have realised my self worth. Ive realised that I took peoples comments very personally. Depression has lifted. And my self confidence is coming back. I am finding myself again as I was totally lost. I cant thank claire enough for her time encouragement & support over the past 3 mths. With her help & support I am slowly getting my life back.

A lady that I work with rang an ambulance at approx 8am. The crew arrived and one of the paramedics came across as arrogant an uncaring and stated that she did not need to go to hospital. She stated that the paramedic wrote her stats wrong on the paperwork and left. Leaving her feeling panicked and really distraught.I spoke to her and suggested we rang her GP who unfortunately wasnt able to offer a telephone consultation until 3.30pm.The GP themselves rang an ambulance as they knew she was quite unwell.It later transpired that she had had a heart attack and was kept in hospital for 5 days.

I suffer from rheumatoid arthritis 23 years now. affecting most joints its also affected my lungs and heart I attend gartnavel general hospital Glasgow under care of Dr hunter and Dr porter both of them are the best doctors consultants on the planet so caring and helpfull

The care here has been excellent there isnt anything that could make it better. The visiting restrictions I find tough. I find this time with the virus is unreal yet I have lived through the 2nd world war and all the difficulties that brought. I miss seeing my family. I can telephone them on my mobile everyday. They have posted in pictures and my great grandchildrens drawings. That was lovely.I pass the time watching TV and reading. The food is good and varied.

I was told to self isolate by my previous job as I used to work in a prison. I felt really bad with it and was worried so phoned 111. The call handler I spoke to was very polite and helpful whilst being efficient. He put my mind at rest.

I was put on co codamol tablets for my migraines 5 years ago, at first I was ok only taking them when I got a migraine and they worked so well, I dont know how it started exactly but over time I loved the feeling codeine tablets gave me. I was always happy they would help me to sleep and make me more confident in life. After 2 years my sister finally noticed my addiction and she rang the doctors, which I was then made an appointment to see a doctor and she put me on anti depressants and just told me to stop taking codeine, I did try I managed a year without them, but then I started again but this time it got worse. I was taking 32 tablets within 2 days. I would get angry and agitated if I never took them, I started having therapy for my anxiety which then I told my story of addiction to my therapist, she then referred me to cgl which I wasnt going to go at first as I didnt think anyone could help me and didnt want anyone taking my happy pills away from me, but I was so worried about the damage it was causing to my body. I was also so numb everyday I was in a world of my own, so I went to my appointment with cgl, and they was great. It didnt take long before they put me on a plan to help me ease of the codeine tablets I always thought I was weird that I was addicted to tablets I thought I was the only one until I started reading up and was amazed there was so many others like me that was addicted to codeine and couldnt see a way out, so Im now on espranor tablets I take 10mg a day And theyre working great.The first 2 weeks I was sick but I couldnt believe that I wasnt even thinking of codeine tablets once on espranor, its been 5 months now and I havent had any codeine I havent once thought about it either and Im such a happier person. I didnt realise what damage it was doing to me I didnt even recognise myself I was numb everyday didnt speak to anyone, always tired, I am so thankful to the cgl team they have been great, even call me once a week to see how I am and just for a chat.Ive also found another way to control my migraines and would never touch a codeine tablet again they ruined me and are just so addictive, I urge anyone that can see there getting addicted to get help straight away, I was a lucky one my blood tests came back ok but my insides could have been damaged a lot more if I would of carried on or I could have overdosed myself, a big thank you to cgl they work so so hard and are there to help anyone who has an addiction, they act more like there your friend than doing a job,

I have found the care here to be excellent. Dont like being moved from one ward to another. I find it difficult initially when my routine is changed. But I have been able to adjust. Not having visitors is not bothering me as I have very few visitors at home.

A was extremely thankful for all your time and effort in keeping in touch via phone call e-mail & skype during these difficult times, she has consistently told me she had full trust in you as an advocate and felt you were fighting her corner. I commenced the online peer to peer groups with Marios about 3 weeks ago. Prior to attending the online group, I was apprehensive, wondering what information will be shared. I was also worried about showing my face, but realizing actually if I didnt, I would not have had the same experience.The people in the group are from all walks of life and what is fascinating is the non judgmental aspect of the meeting. It was really useful and really gave me strength and almost come off the session and more relaxed and calm.Mario is an excellent host. He makes people feel at ease, encourages respect and open conversation. I look forward to actually attending these sessions and feel I come further with each one.Thank you for your support.

We recently had to take our 1 year old to ED as he fell and burst his cheek. The fear and panic I was overwhelming knowing I was taking him into a Covid hot bed. From walking in the front door, the care, compassion and professionalism were second to none. Particularly Nicola. I cant thank them enough for how well they looked after not only my little boy but my husband. They made a traumatic experience for all more relaxed. I will truly always be thankful to our NHS heroes and the ED department at Wishaw deserve praise for what they do day in and day out.

I was recently a patient in ward 119 at RIE. After spending nearly 5 days in the ward after having an elective c-section I have nothing but praise for the fantastic staff who work there. The care both myself and my son received was beyond amazing and completely reassured me after a previous negative birth experience.The staff were warm and compassionate, they were happy to assist with all aspects of care and made me feel relaxed especially when my partner was not able to visit.I enjoyed the peace and certainly felt more relaxed with the current set up of visiting. The staff spent time with me and I truly felt ready for discharge when the day came. At no point did I feel rushed to leave and really couldnt have asked for better care.All the staff are amazing and they have made a very scary time one of the best experiences of my life! Thank you.

l received my Gynaecology OPA after getting referred from my GP , l did think due to the Covid 19 situation , clinic appointments would be suspended . So when l recieved mines really quickly , l was a bit apprehensive and nervous to attend, thinking the worst case senarioBut on arriving my fears went right out the window , Michelle the ANP was lovely as were the other 2 nurses. She explained why l was there , what was going to happen and then what every step of the procedure was and what my options were post procedure.After the procedure , she gave me contact numbers , email address etc if l had any questions . l cant thank her and her team enough for all their help and reassurance today , they made me feel at ease throughout the appointment. As an nurse myself l know how important it is to make the patient feel at ease and they certainly did thathuge thank you again

My little boy has just turned 6 weeks old and I would like to extend my thanks to the wonderful team of midwives we encountered. My community midwife was Lorraine from the Buckie, Keith and Cullen Team and it was like a reunion with an old friend as she had cared for me 4 years prior with pregnancy one. The obvious big change from last pregnancy was the loss of obstetric backup based in Dr Grays Hospital. I was lucky enough to have had a straight forward pregnancy last time was happy to book with Ward 3 on the basis of the positive experience I had encountered there before. Lorraine organised all the routine scans and conducted her routine antenatal care in her usual friendly and reassuring manner sometimes with a student midwife or return to practice midwife present benefiting from her knowledge and experience.The scanning midwives were skilled and patient as my little boy was a bit camera shy on both occasions but they took the time needed to get the information required allowing me to drink more water and move around rather than reschedule appointment when I had already swapped shifts at my work to be there.Then came corona virus and all the necessary changes to service provision that came with it. My last antenatal apppointments were over the phone until I was over my dates. I was anxious to do anything to avoid having to go down to Aberdeen for an induction and especially with the new and necessary restrictions in visiting. Aberdeen was also a good 60 miles away for me, I had a 4 yr old at home and it was spring time - one of the busiest times in the year for my farmer husband. Also, with the country in lockdown this added extra pressure of whether I would have childcare for our 4 yr old or whether I would have to go through the labour on my own.Lorraine saw me at around midday and performed a sweep to try and encourage labour to start and organised post dates scan and induction in case it was required. Fortunately, she worked her magic and I went into ward 3 later that night. The timing was perfect as my 4 yr old was in bed oblivious and our farm worker slept in the spare room at home to be there for him if required. In ward 3 I was met by Midwife Rebecca. I was disappointed in myself that I wasnt as far through the first stage as I thought (or hoped) but Rebecca was quick to remind me that this baby was coming and would be born tonight and that she anticipated that labour would progress quickly from here. She was right (I should have asked her for the lottery numbers when I was in) and was helping me through to the delivery suite about an hour later. She was kind, supportive and kept me going with some added humour and was in control when I was at the stage where I no longer knew what to do with myself and no doubt talking rubbish on the entonox. She called for another midwife when delivery was imminent and Midwife Fiona appeared. She was brilliant too. A calm and reassuring presence who encouraged me over the finish line. She took the baby and did his initial checks while Rebecca was left with a bit of stitching up to do. She did this quickly and skillfully and everything healed with no problems. They also made the best coffee and toast! Husband was back home for a sleep and then able to wake our firstborn to the news he had a wee brother.The next morning midwife Deborah came on shift and did all the usual post natal checks for both me and my baby efficiently even while getting used to the new PPE guidance giving us the green light for discharge home. Follow up with Lorraine and her colleague Kirsty for a weekend visit ensured that initial breast feeding hurdles were overcame.We are grateful to all these amazing ladies for their expert care which we were lucky to have locally. They provide an excellent service in challenging times in a challenging location and are to be applauded!

I was taken ill at work in AprilParamedics arrived and quickly and got me to A&EI had gone into complete Heart block by the time we had arrived the whole team worked extremely hard and I was given CPR 3 times my organs failed but they fought and brought me back I was put on a ventilator and dialysis and taken to ICU when I was woken up 2 days later the Drs nurses and everyone were amazed I had pulled through and didnt have any kind of brain damage.I continued my stay for the next10 days I cannot thank all the team that helped me enough I would not be here today if it wasnt for you all .I am also very honoured that you asked me if you could use my records for training purposes which I am happy for you to do especially if it helps save more livesI am forever in your debt Thankyou all again the NHS are amazing people all of you are so dedicated to what you do.Thankyou again

My wife had a midwifeappointment at Wycombe hospital today. When she got home she was very upset because she felt as though the midwife had treated her like a piece of work that she had to get through and as though the appointment was a tick-box exercise, rather than checking how she and the baby are doing. Not once was she asked how she was. It would have made the world of difference if the midwife had taken two minutes to show an interest and to show that there was someone in the healthcare system who cared about her wellbeing, but that didnt happen.What makes this even more disappointing is that it is really tough for pregnant women and their families in lockdown because they are only able to receive a very limited amount of support from friends and family.It is also Mental Health Awareness week, something that has clearly passed this particular midwife by, and even more of a reason for someone just to ask how my wife was doing. This is the second time my wife has seen this particular midwife and the treatment was the same last time.It is a real shame that my wifehad to experience thisbecause when we had our first baby, the staff at Stoke Mandeville were superb and when we have been on the paediatric wardeveryone has been amazing.

The staff and the doctors at this practice are incredibly friendly and helpful.Ive been registered with the practoce for some time and i must say their knowledge and professionaliam is fantastic.Ive never had trouble getring an appointment and everyone is very accommodating.Its lovely to know that they are willing to go the extra mile for their patients.

Staff worked hard. Was very supportive too. The move went as smooth as it could. What I will say is the floor in my room is that I dont like my room!Otherwise I am well and feel safe & secure on my new ward. I commend staff for coming to work and helping especially in the Covid 19 stages. Thank you Cambridge moved to Carlisle

Struggling with anxiety prior to this service. Husband & daughter finding it hard to cope. IRIS Team came in early February 20 started me with routine & positivity.Together we found ways of helping each other cope with the situation.
Good advice given by all attendants, positive feedback at every stage. The support at the time was valuable and well received.
I am now on the mend thanks to your help. However, there is still a way to go and we are still using a self help course on CBT and using the daily diary to record feelings. 
Thank you to everyone who helped me. Much appreciated.

The move from Cambridge to Carlisle was effortless and over within 2 days, or at least it was for the patients. We caged all our belongings and off they went before us then after dinner on the Sunday we were all took up the stairs to Carlisle and just emptied our cages in our pre determined tooms. The staff had obviously done this before, as you could tell from their efficient way of doing things. It made what could have been a stressful, hard work and upsetting time into an opportunity to see the hospital from a different perspective. The patients now dealt with it as an adventure instead of an upheaval and some have started saying they hope we may stay here for good.
Got seen quickly, Doctor did scan and gave results, told me findings and nothing too worry about, would have appreciated him telling me why i had a fatty lump with connective tissue..

The care we as a family have received from Campbeltown Maternity Unit over the last 9 Months has been phenomenal. There were stressful moments when it looked as though I wouldnt be able to deliver here and of course the restrictions of Covid 19. The thought of having to deliver elsewhere broke my heart. Im a born fighter and wasnt prepared to accept I had no choice. My wonderful midwife arranged a consultant appointment for me with the Consultant I had seen when I had complications after my first labour. A plan was put in place to allow a local delivery on the understanding that if complications arose I would be transferred.Towards the end of March i was experiencing light cramping as the cramps become more rapid it dawned on me they may actually be contractions. We phoned the on call midwife and were advised to go to the Unit, we arrived around midnight. The two midwives on call were Helen & Charlotte. Around 1am my cramps intensified and felt like proper contractions. I asked for gas & air and after an examination my waters broke.The team knew I wanted to use the pool so Charlotte set about filling it. However ourbaby girl wasnt prepared to wait she made a very rapid appearance and was lovingly delivered by Helen around 2.30amI honestly cant fault the care we received in labour and feel so blessed to have a wee Campbeltonian ( even though she was 9lbs 3)My experience of labour here was amazing and Im still a bit overwhelmed by how amazing it was. We look forward to being looked after by these wonderful ladies again in the future when 2 hopefully becomes 3 .Special mention has to be given to how well the midwives have supported all the parents to be in the town during the uncertainty of Covid 19 .Im sure they themselves have at times been scared & worried for their own families .Yet they have gone above & beyond for each and every one of us.Forever grateful

During the Covid 19 outbreak i contacted my doctors with covid symptoms. The reception staff  were very professional and courteous and said a doctor would telephone me. A doctor contacted me within 30 minutes and went through my symptom, deciding I should isolate and get a test as soon as possible. Over the next three weeks, i had three further telephone conversations and was given reassurance and the latest advice in relation to covid 19. The last conversation was initiated by the practice to check up on me and to decide if I needed further investigation into my issues. St. Lukes settled him into a bright room which opened onto a beautiful garden and then he was assessed by a caring doctor. Every day he was washed, as well as once even shaved. The nurses turned him several times a day to make him more comfortable. All this with tremendous care and very good humour. William had severe breathing issues and could no longer take solid food, just a little water. He fought so hard to live but eventually the fight was lost and, 8 days after arriving, my Love & my Life, finally passed. Once again, the staff were tremendous. They provided sympathy, comfort and a lot of tea in my hour of need. I thank everyone at the hospice from the bottom of my heart for the care, and most all, the dignity they gave to my husband of 35 years in his final days. I believe that hospices are hugely undervalued, after all who wants to contemplate their loved ones ever needing this kind of care, let alone consider ever needing it themselves. But should that day come, please remember that St Lukes is only 40% funded by the government, the rest is made up by fund raising and donations and without hospices like St Lukes the world would be a much more difficult place for the terminally ill and their carers.

I had my little boy last summer and have never gotten around to thanking everyone who looked after us both.I opted to deliver in the midwives unit at AMH and was booked in for induction at T+12. I received excellent care from my community midwife Sandra throughout my pregnancy and was scanned at T+7 to check on my babys growth and amniotic levels.With each day over my due date, I felt more apprehensive as I was so overdue and no guarantee when I would be admitted for induction (the process being you were phoned as soon as a spaced became available and T+12 being the earliest date due to being low risk).I naturally went into labour early that morning and attended the assessment unit when my contractions were every 3-5 minutes. Unfortunately I was still in early labour and was sent home. After a few more hours at home I felt I wasnt coping with my labour pains and contractions were less than every 3 minutes so we headed back in. Again I was still in early labour but the midwives reassured me I would not be sent home again. I was offered pain relief and we hired a tens machine. As my labour intensified I was given gas and air (my preference for pain relief) and a swiss ball. My baby was back to back despite my best efforts in the lead up to my due date.I was transferred to labour ward around teatime meeting the day staff. Unfortunately the midwives unit was full. My labour was still slow to progress and my waters were broken to help speed things along. I became hysterical as my waters were stained with meconium (baby had pooped), a sign of foetal distress which I was all too familiar with as a health worker. My baby was monitoring well and the staff tried to put me at ease that this is quite common when babies are over due.I had Senior charge midwife Jenny and staff midwife Michaela looking after me on the night shift who were absolutely amazing. Itwas decided the best thing for me was to have an epidural and hormonal drip as my cervix was swollen, slowing dilation and needed a chance to catch up. I hadnt been keen for an epidural but my birth plan was go with the flow. I am so grateful to Jenny for being to the point with me and helping me agree to an epidural. Once the epidural was in place (big thank you to the anaesthetist!) I was able to think rationally whilst continuing with gas and air. I got some respite between contractions, my labour progressed and I delivered my baby naturally.The only feedback I have is that the seating for birthing partners in labour ward was limited and uncomfortable, and the waiting times/admission for induction process. A chair with arms for my husband and my mum who were my birthing partners to get some rest would have been amazing. They had a hard seat with no arms so were unable to get any rest for 20+ hours.Around my due date there was an exceptionally long wait time for induction which cant be helped. The process for being admitted for induction amplified my anxiety. I felt very fortunate to have gone into labour without induction as waiting would have taken me even further beyond my due date.I cant put into words the appreciation I have for all the care I received throughout my pregnancy.I will especially remember all the kindness and support from Michaela and Jenny. So much love for you guys! And again thank you all for everything.

For a long time I have struggled with my eating. For years I would restrict myself and over the top control in order to loose weight. It was not until I have completely lost control and my eating habits would control my everyday life when I decided I needed help or I would go crazy.I went to my GP and was referred to the St. Georges Community service in Sheffield where I was diagnosed with bulimia, binge eating and body dysmorphia.I started a therapy with Ms. O and could not help her enough. This therapy was for myself very emotion and hard work but after attending a session every week for approx. 2 months I have not only over came the eating disorder but also learned how to accept my body and not allow food control my mood.Before the therapy I would wake up in fear every day thinking wether today I will loose control over food again I would also think about it as a last thing before going to bed. I would fear going out for meals as even one piece of chocolate could trigger a binge. Now all of this is gone.Part of my therapy was planning my meals and sticking to them. I have learned that eating normal will not make me gain weight but make myself and body satisfied and reduce the cravings.I have also done a mirror exposure which helped me with accepting my body and getting rid of the body dysmorphia. Finally I stopped focusing on the issue areas of my body and seen myself as a whole.I eat normal now and can allow myself to have a treat without feeling guilt.I could have never done thins without Ms. O, who has always been here for me wether I had a bad or good week. The therapy sometimes will feel hard and you will feel hopeless but just 2 weeks in you will be able to see more brighter days than before and towards the end you can be completely cured and become a happier person.Also I just would like to add that before binge eating I would weight 10kg less than what I do now but I was less accepting of my body than what I am now!If you struggle with eating just like I have done do not hesitate see a specialist. They know what they are doing and can change your life completely around!

My adult son has Autism and its always a worry when he needs medical care as he has a altered pain perception. We were delighted to receive the Covid 19 Grab & Go for to fill in which would provide information to health care professionals should he need to quickly go to hospital. Importantly this form has an well written guide sheet to help you fill the form in, the suggestion to laminate it was a good one. Whoever thought of this obviously has a good knowledge of patients with additional needs and the importance of taking a holistic approach. Maybe this form could be rolled out for other patients who have additional needs such a neurological conditions or disabilites. Well done Stanmore house for such a patient centered approach.

Your telephone consultation service is excellent. Its very prompt, friendly, professional and competent. I phoned in with my concerns, The receptionist was very helpful and quickly put me in touch with a Nurse Specialist, who took my history connected me with the link to send photos of my lesions and arranged for the doctor to phone me back. The doctor contacted me quite soon, discussed my case and the diagnoses and sent a prescription to the pharmacy. The medicine is effective and the conditions improving. Its all very easy and I imagine if necessary could also be conducted on Zoom or Whatsapp.

While I was in care of the maternity department, the care and attention I received was amazing and cannot in anyway fault the midwives, consultants and doctors. Felt very relaxed and if I had any concerns, I felt I was listened to. Also felt relaxed and calm. I want to thank everyone who looked after me, especially in these new normal times. Keep up the fantastic work.

My stay at the CBU was amazing, talk about a well oiled machine that delivers on its promises...The unit is managed internally amazingly well. This permeates through each member of the various teams which operate in perfect synchronicity. The care afforded by the medical, therapy and domestic teams are second to none in my opinion (which my ego translates into fact... Lol...)I was looked after every step of the way by everyone.My stay at CBU gave me an excellent spring -board into my recovery which is now on going for the rest off my life. Essentially, for me, I wasnt spat out at the other end: the Therapy Team made sure that both they and I were confident that my Exit Plan was water-tight before I left.Ensuring said exit plan was so solid, for me, was the most important part of my -going recovery. Not just for today, but whilst in the unit I was able to detox without fear of relapse and this took off so much pressure and alleviated much of my anxiety.Thank you CBU, you really do deliver...Finally, to say that you were able to remain true to your promises during a time when people were saying that the National Health Service was being brought to its knees, due to this global pandemic, shows how inspirational your work is to this recovering addict.Much loveCarl

Wow, I hadnt visited for some time but had to visit Friday 24 and had a very positive experience, from ringing in and talking to a very friendly and helpful receptionist ,right the way through to seeing  a emphatic,  sincere and thorough doctor.I am so so pleased.

i have been to many surgeries but never seen service so terrible like this. first of all getting to see GP is near to impossible here and even when you get appointment make sure you have rest of your day off as you will have to wait for hours before you are seen. GPs at surgery dont show any care, Receptionists are really unprofessional and rude, they have no respect for you as they will hand up to your face frequently. NHS needs to seriously take notice of this surgery.

I have always found the doctor I see to be extremely good, both medically thorough and kind and courteous.  At this visit for a back problem he facilitated me also having a flu vaccination thus avoiding extra painful visits

I recently joined this practice after having been with my previous practice for over 30 years and seen the gradual deterioration to an extremely poor and inadequate service.  I have been so pleasantly surprised with both the doctors, nurses and reception staff at Norbury Health Centre.  Always so incredibly friendly and caring, the reception staff go out of their way to reassure you and keep an eye that things are running smoothly.  Efficient and informative on every occasion and the doctors have a genuinely interested, caring and professional approach.  So glad I made the move and cant understand why I waited so long.  My daughter has also registered with them now also.  Keep up the good work and many thanks :)

Had my surgery 16th March. Fantastic. All round. Consultant brilliant .skull base nurse brilliant and professional .nothing to much always phoning and checking on me has I was sent home early due to corona virus only. Ward h4 was brilliant to very happy patient
Had  brain surgery in March. Was referred to endocrine  for follow up .excellent care. Lots of communication very proffesional always

My experience of the GPS at this practice has always been positive. Ive found them to be caring and knowledgeable and more than happy to listen to me. There are some issues with making contact with a GP initially, with some of the patient advisors who are the first point of contact being less than helpful. I feel that this is more from a lack of appropriate training than from a desire to prevent patients from speaking to the GPs. The telephone contact system is poor, often with long waits to speak to someone. The econsult form is badly designed with far too much repetition. I recently had to upload photographs via this system and it was very difficult to find where to do this. This needs signposting early in the econsult process. It shouldnt be by trial and error until you find the correct route!

Recently re registered at this practice after having been there for most of my life and Im now shocked at the lack of care offered. Such an impersonal service doctors seem to have little interest or concern to helping. The telephone conversations are always over in a matter of minutes leaving you feeling a inconvenience. Leaving your concerns unaddressed.

Attended with my 10 week old son, the practioner who checked him over was extremly reassuring. He also took the time to explain everything he was doing and was so friendly with my boy that he even made him smile. Thank you for fast efficient and friendly treatment.

I have needed to phone through a few times recently requiring advice or help. The receptionists were helpful gave advice and problem solved. They did not rush me and listened. So often people only comment with complaints I want to praise and thank them. I appreciated all your help. The doctor I spoke to was extremely helpful explained things again did not rush me and was reassuring. Thankyou to that doctor also.

I was treated at NHH as an emergency with a fractured ankle. I had surgery the same day and was discharged the following day. All the staff I met Nurses, Doctors, Health Care Assistants, Radiographers, Porters, and  Domestic were absolutely wonderful. All working with a smile ( behind the mask), lots of reassurance and explanations. Nothing was to much trouble, I was very impressed. As a NHS employee myself, Im a Midwife at another trust, I found my care and treatment faultless. At such a difficult time in hospitals, and some staff working in unfamiliar areas I was proud of the NHS even more. Thank you so much.

We joined this surgery about 6 years ago after relocating to the area. We have always found the Receptionists very helpful, both on the phone and in person. They are very busy and under pressure, but certainly not rude. I do find that generally, If you treat people with respect, its often reciprocated so be nice!The Doctors I have seen have always taken the time to listen to my concerns and work out the appropriate treatment with me.It is true that you cant always get an appointment immediately, but you do always get a call from the Duty Doctor to discuss the problem and if they feel you need to be seen, you will be asked to attend. I am more than happy with the way this works and its more than other practices offer. Sometimes the phone rings for ages and sometimes you are on hold for a while and sometimes you cant get what you want, when you want it, but isnt that just life?!

My mam was rushed into hospital with suspected COVID-19. She tested positive and was also diagnosed with pneumonia. I honestly cant thank the A&E department and Ward 30 for the support and for what they did for my mam. Luckily 4 days of oxygen and antibiotics was enough for her to start to feel better. Thankfully on the 5th day she was discharged. Honestly the most scariest experience - but the staff in hospital were so supportive and helpful even though it must be very very scary for them too. They were even keeping in touch with us at home, letting us know what was happening and any progress. The phone calls we received really put our minds at rest, that progress was happening and mam was getting the right help and support. Thank you so so so much. We didnt think we would get her back home when she left in the ambulance. Stay safe!

Ill admit past experiences of admissions to mental health wards have not always been great for me, I find the environments noisy and distressing. However, on this occasion it was an entirely different experience and I can only praise the staff on Keats Ward, Meadowbrook for their kindness and compassion during my admission. It was ultra distressing (although I dont often show my distress) because for the first time I was Sectioned so everything was taken out of my control. Upon arrival I was showed to my room in which I had to isolate in whilst waiting for a Covid-19 test result to come back. The staff ensured I was ok and fed and watered. My primary nurse talked me through the sectioning process and what my rights where etc. He also took into account my own wants and needs. This experience in Salford was so much better that other admissions Ive had in other towns (Im not from Salford) and I just want to say thanks to the staff for working and caring for patients during these difficult Coronavirus times, you are all stars! Id also like to add the garden on Keats Ward is really impressive and welcoming!
Really friendly helpful surgery. Very good with the patients who have a learning disability whom I support .Saved my husbands life.

I used the e-Consult system for the first time and what an excellent service they gave. The contact information from the Practice was excellent and the advice the GP gave was both helpful and reassuring. All the staff at HEMC are wonderful. Thank you

Evening guys! Im 35 and Ive always had the upmost respect for all the paramedics and NHS staff. Ive never had to use them personally up until Saturday morning when I was awoke with excruciating pain. Rang 111, and an ambulance was sent very quickly. Very friendly paramedics rushed me to the hospital. All the staff at Gloucester Royal Hospital and Cheltenham General hospital have been ace looking after me. Keep up the good work guys, youre doing great!Tim Annis

I am currently being shielded, but was asked to attend today for a blood test.  I was appalled at the total disregard for all safe practices in the current pandemic situation.  On entering the hospital, there was NO hand sanitiser anywhere to be seen, no 2m distancing markings, no signs, and people were walking around in all directions. Once in the department there was absolutely NO social distancing being practiced and no guidance as to how this could be done.  I was even asked, when trying to social distance myself in the corridor, to go into the crowded, disorders waiting room! When patients were being called in, there was no system in place to social distance from the previous.  There were NO windows open anywhere in the department.  Also, when I asked the phlebotomist to clean her hands before putting the needle in my arm, she began arguing with me, saying that she had changed her gloves before I entered the room.  I said that since then she had handled paperwork that Id just handed to her, and that I would be reassured by her cleaning the gloves/hands for me.  She then said, well I could use these wipes and I said, Thank you, Id appreciate that  She begrudging gave them a cursory wipe then proceeded.  I was absolutely appalled by the whole experience and now have to count down the days to find out if I have contracted the virus from my hospital visit today.  Due to my immune system issues, I am someone considered to be clinically extremely vulnerable ... I dont think I need to say anymore.  Thank you for reading
First time I have used E Reception order my repeat prescription because of Covid 19 .Absolutey blown away by how super efficient this service is. Well impressed . Thank you to all involved .

I had both my cataract operations at Spa Medica, Wirral, and would highly recommend them.  My pre-op appointments, the actual operations and the follow up care was excellent and all in a peaceful atmosphere with very professional staff.  Thank you.

Once again, a very good experience at this excellent practice.Friendly, professional, efficient and every proper precaution taken during the virus pandemic.Most reassuring, thank you to everyone there.
I was apprehensive about how useful a virtual appointment would be, but the video call was very good. I was also impressed at being sent the exercises and advice via email.
